# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 78 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 49 | Coptic

---

## Saying 78

**1** Jesus said: "Why have you come out to the countryside? To see a reed shaken by the wind? And to see a man dressed in fine garments like your kings and your great men? Upon them are fine garments, and they are unable to discern the truth."

---

**Translator's Notes (EMET):**

- Parallel to Matthew 11:7-8 / Luke 7:24-25 (the sayings about John the Baptist)
- Thomas omits the identification with John and drops the conclusion about "a prophet"
- "Fine garments" / **ϩⲃⲥⲱ ⲉⲧⲛⲁⲛⲟⲩⲟⲩ** — soft/luxurious clothing
- "Your kings and your great men" — Thomas contextualizes the garments as belonging to the ruling class
- The conclusion "unable to discern the truth" is unique to Thomas — the soft-clothed rulers lack *gnōsis*
- In Q this saying defends John; in Thomas it becomes an anti-worldly power statement
